label: reported
text: According to India Today, the Italian government approved a decree that makes “violent participation in a demonstration” punishable by up to five years in prison and a €20,000 fine, and holds parents financially liable for vandalism committed by their minor children. The measure was introduced after riots in Milan that involved stones thrown at police, looting of shops and damage estimated at over €500,000.

sources.title: Don't burn the house down to prove you are angry - India Today
sources.articleText:
Go to the top of the class, Giorgia Meloni. Good for you. Let me tell you what happened in Milan. Not the sanitised version, but the one that matters. A bunch of people, mostly young, mostly angry about the cost of living, decided that the appropriate response to high fuel prices was to throw stones at police, loot a supermarket, and set fire to scooters near the Duomo.
The Italian government, led by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, responded with the kind of speed that usually gets lost in committees or stays frozen in a pointless threat mode. Within days, a decree was approved: up to five years in prison and a €20,000 fine for "violent participation in a demonstration", with the added proviso of parents being held financially liable for their minor children's acts of vandalism.
